subsystems.name: Global observing system
subsystems.role: supplies the continuous stream of measurements any simulation needs.

subsystems.name: Earth system model
subsystems.role: physically simulates atmosphere, ocean, ice, land and the carbon cycle.

subsystems.name: Human economy model
subsystems.role: represents production, energy use, trade, land use and emissions.

subsystems.name: Data assimilation
subsystems.role: blends live observations with the model so the simulated state matches the real world.

subsystems.name: Compute and software stack
subsystems.role: runs the coupled model fast enough to be useful.

subsystems.name: Uncertainty and decision interface
subsystems.role: turns model output into advice a policymaker can act on.

buildSteps.title: Build and maintain the observing network
buildSteps.detail: Satellites, ocean floats, buoys, flux towers and biodiversity monitoring must report continuously and globally, including over oceans and forests where coverage is thinnest.

buildSteps.title: Standardise the data
buildSteps.detail: Measurements from thousands of instruments are quality-controlled, given common metadata and shared under open formats so models can ingest them automatically.

buildSteps.title: Model each Earth component
buildSteps.detail: Atmosphere, ocean, sea ice, land surface, vegetation and carbon-cycle models are each developed and tested separately.

buildSteps.title: Couple them into one Earth system model
buildSteps.detail: Coupler software exchanges heat, water, carbon and momentum between components at every timestep, so the parts stay physically consistent.

buildSteps.title: Embed the human economy
buildSteps.detail: Energy, agriculture, land-use and trade models are linked to the physical model so that emissions, land clearing and policy choices feed back into the climate.

buildSteps.title: Assimilate live observations
buildSteps.detail: New satellite and ground data are folded into the running model each cycle to keep it anchored to reality rather than drifting.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and validate
buildSteps.detail: The system is replayed against past decades, and against palaeoclimate records, to check it reproduces known change before being used for the future.

buildSteps.title: Scale it to exascale machines
buildSteps.detail: Resolution and ensemble size are increased on the fastest supercomputers; machine-learning emulators stand in for expensive sub-models.

buildSteps.title: Deliver an interactive interface
buildSteps.detail: Users run scenarios and see results with honest uncertainty ranges, not single confident numbers.

prerequisites.why: the first exascale machines ran in 2022; whole-planet simulation at useful resolution needs machines of this class.
satellites provide the routine global coverage that no ground network can.
the CMIP model intercomparison already couples atmosphere, ocean, ice and carbon cycle.
existing models are coarse and treat the economy in aggregated sectors, not as a live system.

prerequisites.tech: Real-time global sensor and data infrastructure
prerequisites.why: coverage of oceans, soils and biodiversity is sparse and data sharing is uneven.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum computers large enough to help
prerequisites.why: today's quantum machines are far too small and error-prone for this workload; classical supercomputers are the realistic path.

pathway.milestone: operational weather forecasting and the CMIP climate projections
pathway.unlocks: seasonal forecasts and long-range climate scenarios, but not an interactive whole-planet twin.

pathway.milestone: kilometre-scale digital twins of weather and climate, such as the EU's Destination Earth initiative
pathway.unlocks: storm-resolving simulation and fast what-if experiments on climate extremes.

pathway.milestone: tight coupling of economy models to Earth system models at seasonal-to-decadal timescales
pathway.unlocks: testing how energy, agriculture and land-use policies feed back into the biosphere.

pathway.milestone: an interactive planetary simulation with quantified uncertainty
pathway.unlocks: policy testing before measures are enacted — if compute, observation coverage and model skill all keep improving.
